agent_priors_used: General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a benchmark comparison is non-identifying unless both a live treatment arm AND non-ceiling baselines exist; measuring per-task economics before the treatment is shipped and the baselines are discriminating yields degenerate or invalid results, so prerequisite repair must precede the flagship run.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): autonomous research lanes drift toward local optima, repeatedly refining a locally measurable instrument while the central decision stays unmade; a concentration/tunnel flag is diagnostic context, never a quota.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): small CPU-quantized LLMs frequently fail structured tool/action emission and multi-step control; supplying the task goal/schema in the system prompt is a known determinant of early-step failure, so model-capability and prompt-underspecification must be separated before concluding a model class is unusable.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a detector validated only against its author's planted surface may not generalize; excluding a known volatile hop-by-hop header (Connection) is a canonical instrumentation fix, and a stability gate must test the frozen quantity, not a stricter composite.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): prerequisite chains (shipped carrier -> discriminating task bank -> capable agent) should be repaired once at the lowest responsible lane rather than rediscovered as MEASUREMENT_INVALID across multiple lanes.

General prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): if fresh-instance acquisition cost grows with site depth there is a persistence break-even surface; if it is flat, the honest architecture treats acquisition as a constant-cost procedure and moves effort to procedure caching and substrate expansion.

allocation.question: Can the already-audited parameterized mechanism carrier be installed byte-identically at the shipping kernel path src/spider/kernel.py, with a binding pre-freeze positive/negative certificate — (a) positive: distill_parameterized over >=3 induction observations -> resolve EXECUTABLE with a correctly bound non-null action at confidence 0.9 -> deterministic fixture execute status 200 -> verify true on an UNSEEN held-out identifier; (b) negative: refuse out-of-support / missing-parameter / wrong-intent bindings with a recorded reason and a null bound action, returning exactly ResolutionStatus.UNKNOWN for the no-applicable-mechanism case; (c) honest inherited-path counters (retrieval_calls, verification_calls, repair_attempts); (d) installed identity equal to the frozen carrier git blob b15ed8487e2d1326df4ca64fb4c7b6e5a0ebf796 / sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72 — such that promotion is enabled ONLY on independent audit PASS, discharging blocker B1?
allocation.rationale: This is audit dependency B1 and readiness condition (1) for the flagship benchmark. The shipped src/spider/kernel.py still creates literal candidates at confidence 0.5 below the default 0.8 execution threshold and lacks distill_parameterized, while a more capable experimental carrier has already been shown causally live, attributable and honestly accounted on a real credential-free HTTP substrate (EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064, audit PASS). The decisive, decision-changing move is to promote that carrier through the audited promotion gate with a known positive AND a known-negative refusal, so the product loop has an executable inherited mechanism that the flagship benchmark can actually exercise. A cognitive reset favors exactly this: a fresh Product seeing today's Codex would not run the four-arm benchmark (which the readiness rule forbids) but would ship the audited carrier. This is readiness condition (1) of three; conditions (2) and (3) are carried by Runtime and Intel, so the flagship C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON runs remain unauthorized this cycle.
